Definition: middle voice from G1223 and G191; to hear throughout, i.e. patiently listen (to a prisoner's plea):--hear.
BiblicalUsage: This word means to hear a man through, to listen patiently to the end of his plea, and it stands once, where Felix promises Paul he will hear him fully when his accusers come. The form in the text is the future of the simpler verb to hear, and it carries the whole weight of a fair hearing.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a patient hearing is the least justice owes a man; Felix promised it and delayed it, but the promise itself is right: every plea deserves to be heard to the end.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
